title: Entropy-aware pager curator and region failover runbooks
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Our current alerting fabric generates high-volume noisy pages during partial region degradations and transient kernel backpressure events. This increases on-call cognitive load and delays correct failover/load-shedding decisions. Goal: Build an entropy-aware pager curator that scores and suppresses noisy signals, ties alerts to SLO delta impact, and automatically coordinates region-aware circuit-breaker and load-shedding runbooks with safe automated actions and human-in-the-loop escalation when needed.
acceptance_criteria: Pager curator computes a per-alert entropy score and risk-weighted priority and exposes an API consumed by PagerDuty/ops routing
Topology-aware failover runbook exists for partial-region SLO degradation with automated pre-checks and safe rollback hooks
Circuit-breaker policy can be toggled via API and console with observable audit trail and metrics (decision latency, suppressed pages, actions executed)
Load-shedding thresholds recommended by runtime analytics are applied in canary, then rolled out automatically with rollback on QoS regressions
Integration tests covering noisy-signal simulation show >=60% reduction in pages to on-call for false-positive scenarios without increasing customer-impacting incidents
implementation_notes: Design a lightweight entropy heuristic combining signal frequency, alert churn, unique-submitters, and correlated metric variance to avoid expensive ML until proven
Tie entropy score to SLO delta estimate: approximate customer_impact = (error_rate_delta * user_traffic_estimate) -> used to override suppression for high-impact alerts
Failover runbooks should include preflight checks: KV cache health, cross-region replication lag, model-variant availability, and recent autoscaler events
Circuit-breaker executor must support staged actions: soft-redirect -> partial shed -> hard-shed, each with automatic monitoring and rollback hooks
Expose observability: suppressed_alerts, suppression_reasons, decision_latency_ms, runbook_step_status, last_rollback_reason
runbook_snippets: On partial-region latency spike (SLO error budget burn > 5% in 10m): 1) run preflight checks (replication_lag < 2s?) 2) increase KV cache replication priority 3) enable single-region routing policy for 5m 4) if errors persist, activate circuit-breaker soft-redirect to replica region

Circuit-breaker steps: soft-redirect (5m) -> monitor 5m -> if CPU qps > threshold then apply token-level shed (10%) -> monitor 10m -> escalate to on-call with context (entropy score, SLO delta, charts) if no improvement
Auto-shed policy includes a safe quota for high-priority customers (whitelist) and per-tenant degrade-to-graceful-failure handlers
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Choice to use heuristic entropy scoring now vs ML: heuristic allows rapid iteration and explainability; ML deferred to Post-MVP after 2 quarters of telemetry
Suppression default set conservatively to avoid masking high-impact alerts; SLO-delta override can force immediate pager for severe cases
Automated actions limited to reversible operations (routing, token-level shed). Destructive operations (node reboots) remain manual
Will implement suppression as a policy layer in the alert router rather than modifying existing alert rules to preserve auditability and revertability
